A doorway other programs use to ask this app for data.

sections.name: Status, Maturity, LifecycleStage, Impact
sections.title: Allowed status and stage words
sections.what: Lists the fixed words allowed for project status, maturity, lifecycle stage and risk impact.
sections.why: Likely reason: it keeps the values consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: A new value on the server must be added here, or screens may not handle it.

sections.name: API_ProjectListItem
sections.title: Project list row
sections.what: Describes the summary of one project: name, description, budget, megawatts, dates, status, likelihood, maturity and lifecycle stage.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list page only needs these summary fields.
sections.watch_out: The budget and end date can be empty, so the screens must handle that.

sections.name: API_EvidenceQuote
sections.title: Evidence quote
sections.what: Describes a quote used as evidence: its text, web address, publisher and date.
sections.why: Likely reason: it lets the app show where a claim came from.
sections.watch_out: The web address can be empty, so links must allow for that.

sections.name: API_Issue
sections.title: Project issue
sections.what: Describes one recorded problem: its lifecycle stage, impact, description, and the IDs of the evidence that supports it.
sections.why: Likely reason: problems must be listed with proof.
sections.watch_out: The lifecycle stage here is plain text rather than the fixed list, so its values are not checked.

sections.name: API_ScorecardPillar
sections.title: Scorecard area
sections.what: Describes one scored area of a project: its score, trend, confidence, positives, negatives, evidence links and matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: it provides a structured assessment for each area.
sections.watch_out: The matches field is typed as any, so its contents are not checked.

sections.name: API_ProjectDetail
sections.title: Full project record
sections.what: Adds to the list row everything the detail page needs: delivery model, risk split, parties, supply chain, cost and schedule variances, similar projects, confidence, issues, scorecard and success story.
sections.why: Likely reason: the detail page needs more than the list shows.
sections.watch_out: The success story can be empty, so callers must check for it before reading it.

sections.name: UI_ProjectListItem
sections.title: Display fields for list rows
sections.what: Declares formatted text fields for budget, megawatts and likelihood, which the screens show in place of raw numbers.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps display formatting separate from the raw data.
sections.watch_out: This file only declares the fields. The code that fills them is not visible here.

sections.name: UI_ProjectDetail
sections.title: Display fields for the detail page
sections.what: Declares a formatted confidence score for the detail page on top of the list display fields.
sections.why: Likely reason: same as the list display fields.
sections.watch_out: The formatting code is not in this file, so the text is only as correct as whatever fills it.

summary: Defines the shapes of project data the server returns, and the extra display fields added for the screens.
purpose: Gives the rest of the app one shared description of project records, their details, risks, scores, and success stories.
why: Likely reason: the names with an API prefix separate raw server data from display data that the screens add. Not stated in the code.
how: It lists the allowed words for status, maturity, lifecycle stage and impact. Then it defines the list row for a project, and a detail record that adds parties, supply chain, cost and schedule variances, similar projects, issues, scorecard and success story. The UI types add formatted text fields for display.
inputs: None at run time. These are compile-time declarations only.
outputs: Type checks in the editor and during the build.
risks: Types do not check real data while the app runs, so a server change can cause silent display problems. One scorecard field is typed as any, so its contents are not checked.
debug: If a value looks wrong on screen, compare the server's reply with the definition here. Compiler errors show mismatches. Check the server version if the reply differs.
